title: [Bugfix request]:  Add LaTeX Rendering Support to JiuWenSwarm Outputs

### 🚀 Background Description


JiuWenSwarm currently does not render LaTeX in its output. Mathematical expressions using formats such as \(...\), \[...\], $...$, and $$...$$ are displayed as raw text, making formulas difficult to read.

Expected behavior:

Render inline formulas, for example: $E = mc^2$

Render block formulas, for example: $$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$$

Support common LaTeX syntax, including fractions, subscripts, superscripts, matrices, and multiline equations

Gracefully fall back to plain text when LaTeX syntax is invalid or incomplete

Use cases:

JiuWenSwarm is often used for mathematical reasoning, algorithm explanations, data analysis, and research-related tasks. Without LaTeX rendering, formulas are harder to understand and verify.

Suggested implementation:

Integrate a LaTeX rendering library such as KaTeX or MathJax into the existing Markdown output pipeline.

Acceptance criteria:

Inline and block-level LaTeX formulas render correctly.

Regular Markdown rendering remains unaffected.

Dollar signs and LaTeX-like content inside code blocks are not rendered as formulas.

Invalid LaTeX does not cause the entire output area to fail.

title: [Feature]: openJiuwen supports the collection of structured execution traces of agents.
body:
### 🚀 Background Description


The current openJiuwen system generates an excessive volume of log data that is disorganised and lacks a coherent view of the agent's internal workflow. Operators and developers cannot easily discern which steps the agent took, which tools were invoked, the parameters passed, or the outcomes of each action. This opacity complicates debugging, performance tuning, and user-behaviour analysis. To enable effective monitoring and root-cause investigation, we need a dedicated mechanism that collects the complete execution trace of each agent session in a structured, queryable, and human-readable format.

### Design Ideas

We will implement a trace collector that records every atomic unit of work during an agent interaction, including the user query, internal reasoning snippets, tool selection decisions, input arguments, raw outputs, timestamps, and any error states. All traces are serialised as JSON and stored in a central repository (e.g., Elasticsearch) with session‑level indexing and a unique trace ID. A companion dashboard will allow operators to replay any session step by step, filter by tool type or duration, and identify bottlenecks or unexpected loops, turning raw logs into actionable insights.

### Involved Public APIs

_No response_

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

_No response_

### Test Design and Test Plan

Testing will validate completeness, correctness, and performance. We will run a predefined set of test dialogues covering common and edge cases, then compare the captured traces against the expected step sequences to ensure every tool call and its response is logged accurately with correct parameters. We also inject faults such as tool timeouts or invalid inputs to verify that error traces are fully captured. Finally, we conduct load tests with hundreds of concurrent sessions to measure trace ingestion latency and storage overhead, confirming they stay within acceptable limits while preserving full fidelity for retrospective analysis.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

- I launched jiuwenswarm-start without first correctly building the frontend. The process terminated as expected, but when launching again, I observed it was not launching on the default ports 18092 / 19000 / 19001/ 5173.
- The cause of this behavior is a bug in which the teardown leaves orphan processes that stayed occupying some of the ports above.
- The root cause is the fact that when it receives a signal, the python interpreter shuts down immediately and did not run the finally block with the _terminate_all call in app.py
- The solution involves capturing these signals to be able to gracefully terminate the program rather than propagating it to the Python interpreter

title: [Bug]:  `jiuwenswarm --version` fails with "unrecognized arguments" although the docs recommend it for bug reports
body:
Paired: [GitHub #9887](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/issues/9887) ↔ [GitCode #5912](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/5912)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

`docs/en/InstallGuide.md` (FAQ: "How do I check the installed version?") and `docs/en/Contributing.md` (bug report checklist) tell users to run `jiuwenswarm --version`, but the command fails:

```
$ uv run jiuwenswarm --version
usage: jiuwenswarm chat [-h] [--mode MODE] [--session SESSION] [--cwd CWD] ...
jiuwenswarm chat: error: unrecognized arguments: --version
```

The `jiuwenswarm` entry point (`jiuwenswarm.channels.cli.main:main`) appears to route the arguments to the default `chat` subcommand, which has no `--version` option. As a result there is no CLI way to print the installed version, and contributors following the bug report checklist hit this error.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Install from source (`uv sync`) or via pip.
2. Run `jiuwenswarm --version`.

**Expected:** prints the installed version (e.g. `jiuwenswarm 0.2.5.beta1`) and exits with code 0.
**Actual:** argparse error from the `chat` subcommand, exit code 2.

**Suggested fix:** add a top-level `--version` option that prints the installed package version. I'd like to work on this.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
- Python: 3.11.17 (uv-managed venv)
- Install method: source install from develop

### Additional Information

Found while filling in the version field for [#5803](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/5803) and [#5804](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/5804).

title: [Feature]: Heartbeat mechanisms are implanted into jiuwenswarm to support daily life monitoring.
body:
### 🚀 Background Description


The current jiuwenswarm system lacks any active client‑side heartbeat reporting, leaving the operations team unable to track daily active users or measure user growth effectively. Without reliable session data, retention analysis and campaign performance evaluation become guesswork. Introducing a periodic heartbeat mechanism will allow the server to record each client's online presence at fixed intervals, creating the essential data pipeline for DAU statistics and supporting data‑driven decisions on product improvements and marketing investments.

### Design Ideas

We will implement a client‑server heartbeat protocol where each client sends a lightweight payload (including device ID, timestamp, and version info) to a dedicated server endpoint every 30 seconds (configurable). The server processes these heartbeats by updating a Redis‑based last‑seen record and incrementing a daily counter for that user. A scheduled batch job runs at midnight to aggregate all unique user IDs with activity in the past 24 hours, producing the official DAU figure, which is then stored for historical trend analysis and exposed via a simple reporting API for operations to query.

### Involved Public APIs

_No response_

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

_No response_

### Test Design and Test Plan

Testing will cover functional correctness, timing accuracy, and resilience. We will launch multiple emulated clients and inspect server logs to ensure every heartbeat is received and the active timestamp updates correctly. Then we will fast‑forward the system clock to trigger the daily aggregation and validate the resulting DAU count against the raw heartbeat entries. We also need to simulate network partitions, client crashes, and high‑load scenarios (e.g., 10k concurrent clients) to confirm that the reconnection logic works without overcounting or losing events, and that the aggregation handles timezone shifts and duplicate submissions gracefully.

title: [Feature]: Integrate AgentDropoutV2 rectify-or-reject pruning paradigm into JiuwenSwarm team mode
body:
### 🚀 Background Description


======EN======
In the team or cluster mode, multiple agents (leader plus teammates) collaborate by sharing contributions through team messaging mechanisms such as team.send_message. However, it is possible for a teammate to be inefficient, provide incorrect outputs, or even act in an adversarial or manipulative manner. If these erroneous outputs persistently enter the shared team context, the entire group may deviate from the correct solution, and the ultimate goal could be corrupted by bad inputs from specific agents within the group. To address this, AgentDropoutV2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23258) proposes a solution that intercepts an agent's output before it is broadcast, audits it against failure indicators, provides targeted rectification feedback upon detection, and rejects, drops, or removes the agent if it continues to fail even after correction.

======ZH======
在团队或集群模式下，多个智能体（领导者与队友）通过团队消息机制（如 team.send_message）共享各自贡献来进行协作。然而，队友可能会出现效率低下、输出错误，甚至表现出对抗性或操纵性行为。如果这些错误输出持续进入共享的团队上下文，整个团队可能会偏离正确解决方案，且最终目标可能因团队中特定智能体提供的不良输入而被破坏。为解决这一问题，AgentDropoutV2（ https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23258 ）提出了一种解决方案，该方案在智能体输出被广播之前对其进行拦截，根据故障指标进行审计，并在检测后提供针对性的修正反馈；如果智能体在修正后仍持续失败，则将其拒绝、丢弃或移除。


### Design Ideas

A dedicated `jiuwenswarm/agents/dropout/` module where the agent dropout strategies could be gathered and also extended in future.

title: [Mirror] openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm#412 [RFC]: Unify exception hierarchies under the openjiuwen taxonomy and add boundary error telemetry
body:
### Background and Goal Description
            
The repo has ~1,750 except Exception blocks and three unrelated exception
hierarchies (TeamError, A2XError, LLMClientError), none carrying stable
error codes or recoverable/fatal semantics. Boundary failures (agent stream task,
gateway message loop, A2A executor, scheduler) are logged but invisible in traces,
so production incidents can't be diagnosed from telemetry — reproducing the run is
the only way to see the original exception.

The pinned openjiuwen already ships the unified taxonomy (BaseError +
StatusCode) and team_observability OTel tracing is now enabled by default —
neither is being used for app-level errors.
### Proposed Solution
            
Bridge app errors onto the SDK taxonomy: new jiuwenswarm/common/errors.py
with JiuwenError(BaseError) (message-first constructor, call sites unchanged),
and re-parent the three hierarchies under it.
Record boundary exceptions on OTel spans via a never-raising helper at the four
designated boundaries; everywhere else catch specific types.
Enforce locally with semgrep rules + a count ratchet (no CI wiring yet, per
team decision).
### Involved Public APIs
            

### Test Verification
            
Compatibility: existing exception behavior unchanged — str(TeamCreateError("boom")) == "boom", constructors and pickling work, one except BaseError catches
TeamError/A2XError/LLMClientError alike.
Functional: with default config (team_observability on, file exporter), a forced
failure at any boundary (stream task, gateway loop, A2A execute, scheduler) produces
a span with the recorded exception in the trace file, and existing error responses
to clients are unchanged.
Enforcement: python scripts/check_except_baseline.py exits 0 at baseline, 1 on
any new broad catch; semgrep rules flag silent swallows.

title: JiuwenBox build disables TLS and package-signature verification
body:
Paired: [GitHub #7738](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/issues/7738) ↔ [GitCode #5037](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/5037)

## Summary

jiuwenbox/docker/Dockerfile disables yum repository TLS verification (`sslverify=false`), sets curl to accept invalid TLS globally for the build user (`~/.curlrc` with `insecure`), and disables RPM GPG signature checking (`gpgcheck=0`) before installing system packages (bubblewrap, iptables, nftables, java, nodejs, git, etc.):

```
RUN echo "sslverify=false" >> /etc/yum.conf
RUN echo "insecure" >> ~/.curlrc
RUN sed -i 's/gpgcheck=1/gpgcheck=0/g' /etc/yum.conf /etc/yum.repos.d/openEuler.repo
```

## Impact

A MITM on the build network, or a compromised or typosquatted mirror, could inject arbitrary unsigned packages into the resulting image, since neither the transport nor the package signatures are verified during the build.

## Affected version

Confirmed on current `develop` HEAD.

## Suggested fix

Remove the three lines. A fix is attached as a PR, verified by building the image successfully with the real openEuler/yum mirrors without them, so the disabling does not appear to be required.

title: [Feature]: Bring the JiuwenSwarm Agent into the IDE
body:
Paired: [GitHub #4105](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/issues/4105) ↔ [GitCode #3550](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/3550) ### 🚀 Background Description JiuwenSwarm serves knowledge workers whose thinking happens in code, with the file and project as their raw material. But the agent lives in a separate web app. Using it on the code the developer is actually editing forces a manual, disconnected flow: - **Copy-paste as the transport layer.** Select code, switch to the web app, paste it, lose the surrounding file/project context, then repeat for every file. A change spanning three files becomes three round-trips of copying. - **No memory of the project.** The agent never sees the active file, the selection, the diagnostics, or the project tree. Context the developer can see — the surrounding function, the import, the failing test — has to be described back in prose. - **No action on the code.** Even when the agent has a useful answer, it cannot edit the file, open the diff, run the command, or jump to the symbol. The answer arrives in a chat window disconnected from the thing it is about. ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef fail fill:#FFCDD2,color:#111,stroke:#C62828 classDef plain fill:#ECEFF1,color:#111,stroke:#607D8B DEV(["developer coding in the IDE
(fix, refactor, understand)"]):::plain DEV -->|"copy code + describe file, diagnostics,
project tree in prose"| APP["agent in the web app
no access to the codebase"]:::fail APP -->|"generic answer — cannot edit/run/diff"| BACK["dev pastes back, applies by hand, re-runs"]:::fail BACK -->|"new error, repeat per file"| UNHAPPY(["developer stuck in a
disconnected fix loop"]):::fail ``` ### Design Ideas ### Proposed design Two IDE plugins (JetBrains + VS Code) sharing one webview chat UI and one real-time protocol, shipped as the `channels/ide/` channel in the JiuwenSwarm repository, alongside the existing `web` / `tui` / `acp` / `desktop` channels: - **Shared webview chat panel** (`shared-webview`) — a self-contained HTML/JS chat UI embedded via JCEF in JetBrains and as a webview in VS Code, so both IDEs render an identical interface. - **Streaming chat panel** — the agent response streams token-by-token with Markdown rendering, thinking blocks, and tool-call cards. - **IDE context injection** — every message automatically includes the active file path + language, cursor line, selected code, editor diagnostics, other open tabs, project tree, git branch/status, and project rules (`AGENTS.md` / `.jiuwenswarm/`). - **File edit workflow** — the agent edits files through a side-by-side diff review (JetBrains) or VS Code's diff viewer, with optional approval and auto-apply; checkpoint/rewind restores a turn's changes. - **Terminal integration** — agent shell commands run in a dedicated IDE terminal tab so output is visible and scrollable. - **Swarm Map** — a real-time visual overview of `code.team` sessions (Map / List / Board), showing each worker agent's task, status, and activity. - **Session management** — create, switch, delete, resume named sessions; sessions share history with the webview. **IDE-side agent tools** (dispatched by the IDE when the server sends a `tool_call` envelope): | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `str_replace_editor` | Apply a targeted string replacement to a file | | `write_file` / `create_file` | Write or create a file in the workspace | | `bash` / `run_command` | Run a shell command in the IDE terminal | | `read_file` | Read a file from the workspace | | `web_search` / `todo_write` | Search the web / track TODOs | ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef ok fill:#BBDEFB,color:#111,stroke:#1565C0 classDef done fill:#C8E6C9,color:#111,stroke:#2E7D32 classDef plain fill:#ECEFF1,color:#111,stroke:#607D8B DEV(["developer coding in the IDE"]):::plain DEV -->|"plugin injects active file, selection,
diagnostics, project tree"| BG["WebSocket to JiuwenSwarm
channel_id: ide"]:::ok BG -->|"agent sees the codebase, streams reply"| PANEL["IDE chat panel (shared webview)"]:::ok PANEL -->|"agent edits files, runs commands"| TOOLS["IDE tools
(diff review, terminal)"]:::done TOOLS -->|"changes applied in the IDE"| HAPPY(["developer stays in flow"]):::done ``` ### Involved Public APIs New components added under `channels/ide/packages/` in the JiuwenSwarm repository: | API | Kind | |---|---| | `vscode-extension/` | new package (VS Code extension, TypeScript + esbuild) | | `jetbrains-plugin/` | new package (JetBrains plugin, Kotlin + Gradle) | | `shared-webview/` | new package (shared chat UI: `chat.html`, `swarm_map.html`, `icon.svg`) | | `WsClient` | new class (WebSocket client, exponential back-off reconnect, `channel_id: "ide"`) | | `SessionManager` | new class (session lifecycle, server as source of truth) | | `ContextCollector` | new class (IDE context injection: active file, selection, diagnostics, project tree, git, project rules) | | `DiffApplier` / `DiffViewer` | new classes (file-edit diff review + apply) | | `TerminalManager` | new class (agent commands routed to an IDE terminal) | | `SwarmState` / `SwarmMapPanel` | new classes (team-session visualisation) | | `StatusBar` | new class (connection state, token usage, active agent count) | | `ChatPanel` | new class (streaming chat UI over the shared webview) | **Impact:** additive. The channel is added to the JiuwenSwarm repository (`channels/ide/`) with its user docs (`docs/{en,zh}/ide/`) and docs-index updates. Both plugins are **clients of the existing JiuwenSwarm WebSocket gateway** (`channel_id: "ide"`, same protocol as the web UI) — the agent runtime and server API are unchanged. Sessions created by the plugins are stored server-side and immediately shared with the webview and other channels. ### Description of Relevance to Other Modules - **`channels/ide/`** — the new channel (workspace root + `publishing/`). - **`channels/ide/packages/vscode-extension/`** — `WsClient`, `SessionManager`, `ContextCollector`, `DiffViewer`, `DiffApplier`, `TerminalManager`, `SwarmState`, `SwarmStateManager`, `ChatPanel`, `StatusBar`, code-action quick fix. - **`channels/ide/packages/jetbrains-plugin/`** — Kotlin equivalents (tool window, JCEF webview, diff apply, terminal, status bar widget, Alt+Enter quick fix). - **`channels/ide/packages/shared-webview/`** — the shared chat UI embedded by both plugins. - **JiuwenSwarm server** — unchanged; both plugins are gateway clients, so sessions are stored server-side and immediately visible in the web app. ### Test Design and Test Plan Unit/integration tests: 1. **WebSocket client** — connects, and reconnects with exponential back-off after the service worker / extension host restarts. 2. **Session management** — create, switch, delete, and resume named sessions; the server remains the source of truth. 3. **IDE context injection** — the active file path + language, cursor line, selected code, diagnostics, project tree, git branch/status, and project rules are included in each message. 4. **File edits** — `str_replace_editor`, `write_file`, `create_file` apply via diff review / auto-apply and are undoable (rewind restores a turn). 5. **Terminal** — agent `bash` / `run_command` output is shown in the IDE terminal. 6. **Tools** — each IDE tool produces the correct result and surfaces errors (e.g. write to a non-existent path) as tool results. 7. **Context continuity** — a session started in the IDE is the same session in the web app. 8. **Swarm Map** — `code.team` sessions render live agent activity (member, task, message events). Performance/reliability: - **Chat stays responsive** — streaming renders per-frame; large replies do not block the editor. ### Additional Information _No response_

title: JiuwenBox Unix socket defaults to world-writable management access
body:
Paired: [GitHub #7740](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/issues/7740) ↔ [GitCode #5038](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/5038)

## Summary

jiuwenbox's `_chmod_uds_socket_if_any()` (jiuwenbox/src/jiuwenbox/server/app.py) reads `JIUWENBOX_UDS_MODE` with a default of `"0666"` (world read+write) and applies it to the UDS socket file whenever `JIUWENBOX_UDS_PATH` is configured. Authentication is controlled by a separate env var (`JIUWENBOX_API_TOKEN`) unrelated to the socket's own filesystem permissions.

## Impact

Running jiuwenbox in UDS mode with no token configured and the default socket mode, any local user on the host who can reach the socket file gets full unauthenticated access to sandbox exec, policy, proxy, and MCP operations, the same execution capability as the network-bind finding in [#5036](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/5036), reachable via a local socket instead of a network port.

## Affected version

Confirmed on current `develop` HEAD.

## Suggested fix

Default `JIUWENBOX_UDS_MODE` to `0600` (owner-only) instead of `0666`. An operator who wants a shared socket for a legitimate multi-process-same-user deployment can still set it explicitly. A fix is attached as a PR.

I take inspiration from the permission systems of OpenClaw and DeepSeek Harness. I think we can improve on the current permission level system, which only has "Default" and "Full Access". Specifically, I suggest the following permission levels

title: [Feature]: Bring the JiuwenSwarm Agent into the Browser
body:
## Background Description JiuwenSwarm serves knowledge workers whose thinking happens in the browser, with the web page they are reading as their raw material — a paper on arXiv, an SEC filing, a PubMed abstract, a Twitter thread, a GitHub PR. But the agent lives in a separate web app. Using it on anything the user is reading forces a manual, disconnected flow: - **Copy-paste as the transport layer.** Select text, switch to the web app, paste it, lose the surrounding context, then repeat for every additional page. A question spanning three tabs becomes three round-trips of copying. - **No memory of the page.** The agent never sees the page the user is actually looking at. Context the user can see — where a figure sits, what a highlighted passage says — has to be described back in prose. - **No action on the page.** Even when the agent has a useful answer, it cannot point at the page, highlight the passage it is citing, or fill the form the user was filling. The answer arrives in a chat window disconnected from the thing it is about. ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef fail fill:#FFCDD2,color:#111,stroke:#C62828 classDef plain fill:#ECEFF1,color:#111,stroke:#607D8B PAGE(["user reads a web page
(arXiv, SEC, PubMed, GitHub)"]):::plain PAGE -->|"select + copy"| COPY["switch to web app, paste
lose surrounding context"]:::fail COPY -->|"per tab, repeatedly "| UNHAPPY(["user is stuck copy-pasting,
agent can't see or act on the page"]):::fail ``` ## Design Ideas ### Proposed design A Chrome extension (Manifest V3) with four runtime layers that connect to the existing JiuwenSwarm WebSocket gateway. The channel ships as `channels/browser/` in the JiuwenSwarm repository, alongside the existing `web` / `tui` / `acp` / `desktop` channels: - **Layer 1 — Background service worker.** The central hub, running separately from both the page and the side panel. Maintains the WebSocket connection, session lifecycle, page-context cache, tab tracking, right-click menu, panel opening, and a browser-native tool dispatcher. - **Layer 2 — Content script.** Injected into every web page; detects the page type, routes to one of nine page-type extractors (8 adapters + Readability.js fallback), extracts text (head+tail, capped at 120,000 chars), tracks selection, and responds to highlight/scroll/fill commands from the background. - **Layer 3 — Side panel.** A persistent Chrome Side Panel beside the page: native streaming chat, session picker, context bar with pinned-page chips, reader view, tour, privacy disclosure, and full-text search. - **Layer 4 — Popup and options.** A toolbar connection-status popup and a settings page for the server host, port, default mode, and behaviour toggles. **Browser-native agent tools** (8) dispatched by the background worker when the server sends a `tool_call` envelope: | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `get_selection` | Read current text selection in the active tab | | `highlight_text` | Highlight a passage in the active tab with a colored overlay | | `fill_form` | Fill form fields in the active tab by label or field name | | `scroll_to` | Scroll the active tab to a CSS selector | | `take_screenshot` | Capture the visible area of the active tab as a base64 PNG | | `open_url` | Open a URL in a new tab | | `read_page` | Extract text from a tab by URL, or the active tab if no URL given | | `pin_page` | Pin the current tab to the active research session | ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef ok fill:#BBDEFB,color:#111,stroke:#1565C0 classDef done fill:#C8E6C9,color:#111,stroke:#2E7D32 classDef plain fill:#ECEFF1,color:#111,stroke:#607D8B PAGE(["user reads a web page
(arXiv, SEC, PubMed, GitHub)"]):::plain PAGE -->|"content script extracts,
pins page context"| BG["background service worker
WebSocket to JiuwenSwarm"]:::ok BG -->|"agent sees the page, streams reply"| PANEL["side panel chat"]:::ok PANEL -->|"agent highlights, fills, scrolls"| TOOLS["browser-native tools
(highlight, fill, scroll, ...)"]:::done TOOLS -->|"acts on the page "| HAPPY(["user stays focused on the page"]):::done ``` ## Involved Public APIs New components added under `channels/browser/frontend/src/` in the JiuwenSwarm repository: | API | Kind | |---|---| | `WsClient` | new class (WebSocket client, exponential back-off reconnect) | | `SessionManager` | new class (research session lifecycle, server as source of truth) | | `ContextCache` | new class (per-tab page-context cache) | | `TabWatcher` | new class (tab lifecycle tracking, re-extraction on navigation) | | `ToolDispatcher` | new class (dispatch the 8 browser-native tools) | | `Extractor` + `PageTypeDetector` | new classes (page text extraction + type routing) | | 9 page-type extractors | new modules (GitHub, arXiv, SEC EDGAR, PubMed, Wikipedia, YouTube, Twitter/X, Hacker News, Readability.js fallback) | | `ChatBridge`, `SessionPicker`, `ContextBar`, `SessionExporter` | new side-panel components | | `chat`, `markdown`, `reader`, `tour`, `privacy`, `search` | new side-panel modules | | `protocol` / message types | new module (content ↔ background ↔ side-panel wire protocol) | **Impact:** additive. The channel is added to the JiuwenSwarm repository (`channels/browser/`) with its user docs (`docs/{en,zh}/browser-extension/`) and docs-index updates. The extension is a **client of the existing JiuwenSwarm WebSocket gateway** (same protocol as the web UI and IDE plugin) — the agent runtime and server API are unchanged. Sessions created by the extension are stored server-side and immediately shared with the webview and other channels. ## Description of Relevance to Other Modules - **`channels/browser/`** — the new channel (frontend extension + `publishing/`). - **`channels/browser/frontend/background/`** — `WsClient`, `SessionManager`, `ContextCache`, `TabWatcher`, `ContextMenu`, `PanelManager`, `ToolDispatcher`. - **`channels/browser/frontend/content/`** — `Extractor`, `PageTypeDetector`, 9 extractors, `SelectionMonitor`, `Annotator`, `FormAssist`. - **`channels/browser/frontend/sidepanel/`** — `ChatBridge`, `SessionPicker`, `ContextBar`, `SessionExporter`, `chat`, `markdown`, `reader`, `tour`, `privacy`, `search`, native chat. - **`channels/browser/frontend/popup/` + `options/`** — connection status and settings. - **`channels/browser/frontend/shared/`** — types, protocol, storage, constants shared across the three contexts. - **JiuwenSwarm server** — unchanged; the extension is a gateway client, so sessions are stored server-side and immediately visible in the web app. ## Test Design and Test Plan Unit/integration tests: 1. **WebSocket client** — connects, and reconnects with exponential back-off after the MV3 service worker terminates and wakes. 2. **Session management** — create, switch, and resume research sessions; the active pointer is persisted and the server remains the source of truth. 3. **Page extraction** — the correct page-type extractor is selected; generic article pages fall back to Readability.js; output is head+tail truncated to the 120,000-char cap. 4. **Adapters** — each extractor returns the expected structured content for its site. 5. **Tools** — `get_selection`, `highlight_text`, `fill_form`, `scroll_to`, `take_screenshot`, `open_url`, `read_page`, and `pin_page` each produce the correct result and surface errors (e.g. screenshot on a background/minimized window) as tool results. 6. **Cross-page session** — a question spanning multiple pinned pages is answered using all pinned contexts. 7. **Context continuity** — a session started in the browser is the same session in the web app. 8. **Service-worker sleep** — an in-flight `tool_call` dispatched while the worker is asleep generates a contained error response, and reconnects on wake. Performance/reliability: - **Extraction does not block rendering** — the content script runs at `document_idle`; large-page extraction stays bounded by the char cap.

title: [Feature]: [E6] Email/SMTP channel — reach users without an IM platform
body:
### 🚀 Background Description


Ticket E6 (Epic E — Channels & Distribution). Depends on E1 ([#2979](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/2979)) and E2 ([#3061](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/3061)).

`config.yaml` already carries an `email_settings` block (address, token,
smtp_server, port) but no code reads it: there is no email adapter. Every
existing channel is an instant-messaging platform, so a user without Slack,
Discord or Feishu has no way to reach the agent.

Email is also the sharpest test of the connector SDK: no buttons, no
streaming, no native threads. An interactive card must arrive as readable
numbered-reply text (E2 degradation) and the reply must map back to the card
action.

### Design Ideas

Stacked slices, additive first:
1. E6-a — pure `email_format.py`: `normalize_subject()`, `reply_subject()`,
   `thread_key()`, `strip_quoted_reply()`. No network, fully unit-tested.
2. E6-b — `EmailChannel(BaseChannel)`: SMTP send, `ChannelCapabilities` with
   every flag False so E2 degradation applies, session id per thread key.
3. E6-c — IMAP polling inbound, router wiring, config and docs.

title: [Hack the North 2026] openJiuwen Multi-Agent Challenge
body:
Paired: [GitHub #3067](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/issues/3067) ↔ [GitCode #3193](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/3193)

# openJiuwen Multi-Agent Challenge: Build Collaborative Agents That Get Things Done

## Sponsor API Credits

To access the sponsored API credits, please apply on https://luma.com/mc7lijgs :

Please note that:

1. We provide API Credit through OpenRouter, check out more at OpenRouter docs.

2. Each team may apply **only once**. Please do not submit duplicate requests.

3. A total of **200 API keys** are available and will be distributed on a **first-come, first-served basis while supplies last**.

4. Upon approval, you will receive an email with api key in it. The limit would be 40 USD.

5. Teams that receive the sponsored API credit are expected to **submit their project to the Huawei openJiuwen Multi-Agent Challenge track**.

## Brief Introduction

AI agents are moving beyond single-agent assistants toward **teams of specialized agents that can collaborate to solve complex tasks**.

The **openJiuwen Multi-Agent Challenge** asks hackers to build a functional multi-agent AI application that solves a meaningful real-world problem through intelligent agent collaboration.

Your system should go beyond simply calling multiple agents or chaining several LLM prompts together. We want to see agents that can **divide responsibilities, communicate, coordinate, use tools and Skills, adapt to intermediate results, and work together toward a shared goal**.

Teams are encouraged to explore capabilities such as:

● **Task decomposition** — break a complex goal into meaningful subtasks

● **Role specialization** — assign different responsibilities, expertise, or perspectives to different agents

● **Agent communication** — exchange information, intermediate outputs, requests, or feedback

● **Tool and Skill invocation** — allow agents to interact with external tools, APIs, code, files, or reusable Skills

● **Dynamic coordination** — adjust plans, assignments, or execution based on intermediate results

● **Parallel execution** — run independent workstreams concurrently where appropriate

● **Result verification** — review, critique, validate, or cross-check outputs before producing the final result

● **Failure handling** — recover, retry, reassign, or degrade gracefully when an agent or tool fails

● **Reusable collaboration patterns** — capture successful multi-agent workflows so they can be applied to similar tasks again

Applications may target scenarios such as:

● Enterprise workflows

● Research and knowledge work

● Software development and coding

● Data analysis

● Personal productivity

● Education

● Creative collaboration

● Planning and decision support

● Scientific or technical workflows

● Other innovative multi-agent applications

You do **not** need to demonstrate every capability listed above. A focused application with a clear reason for using multiple collaborating agents is better than an overly complicated system.

**Participants are encouraged to build on or extend **[**JiuwenSwarm**](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm)** as the reference multi-agent framework.**

**Note: The latest official version of JiuwenSwarm has been upgraded to **[**WorkSwarm**](https://openjiuwen.com/en/workswarm)**. Participants are encouraged to review and use the latest WorkSwarm release where appropriate. JiuwenSwarm remains relevant as the original reference framework and documentation context for this challenge.**

JiuwenSwarm supports Leader-driven task decomposition, specialized teammates, dynamic multi-agent collaboration, tool invocation, Skills, distributed execution, and reusable Swarm collaboration workflows. The upgraded WorkSwarm project continues this direction with the latest official framework updates.

Teams may choose between two implementation paths:

● **Create a reusable Swarm Skill** using JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm. This path is suitable for teams that want to package a general-purpose multi-agent collaboration pattern that can be reused across similar tasks.

● **Directly implement a customized multi-agent application** on top of JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm. This path is suitable for teams that want to focus on building a complete application tailored to a specific real-world scenario.

Both paths are fully valid for the challenge. A Swarm Skill is not required, but teams are encouraged to consider whether their collaboration workflow could be generalized and packaged for reuse.

**Full challenge details, sponsored API credits, technical guidance, examples, and resources:**
[openJiuwen Multi-Agent Challenge · GitHub](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/issues/3067)

---

## Prize Description

The **openJiuwen Multi-Agent Sponsor Prize** recognizes teams that build the most compelling AI applications through meaningful multi-agent collaboration.

### 1st Place

Each member of the 1st-place team will receive:

● **Huawei Watch GT 6**

● An **internship opportunity with the openJiuwen team at the Huawei Toronto Research Center**, available to exceptional candidates following an interview process

### 2nd Place

Each member of the 2nd-place team will receive:

● **Huawei FreeClip 2 Earbuds**

● A **exclusive office tour of the Huawei Toronto Research Center**

Winning teams will be selected based on the quality of their application, multi-agent collaboration design, technical implementation, demo completeness, creativity, and potential real-world impact.

The internship opportunity is intended for exceptional candidates who demonstrate outstanding technical ability, creativity, initiative, and a strong understanding of multi-agent systems. Candidates may be invited to participate in interviews with the openJiuwen team at the Huawei Toronto Research Center. The opportunity is subject to interview performance, candidate qualifications, eligibility, availability, and applicable internship requirements.

---

## Sponsored API Credits

Each participating team may receive up to:

### **$40 USD in API credits per team**

The credits are intended to support model API calls during development and testing of the hackathon project.

Teams may use the sponsored credits to experiment with agent roles, multi-agent workflows, tool calls, reasoning, evaluation, and other components of their application.

**Conditions apply.** Detailed instructions regarding API access and credit usage will be provided through the challenge resources or by the challenge organizers.

---

## Eligibility

To be eligible for the **openJiuwen Multi-Agent Sponsor Prize**, your team must:

● Build a **functional and demo-ready multi-agent AI application** during Hack the North.

● Use **multiple AI agents or clearly separated agent roles** that collaborate toward a shared objective.

● Demonstrate a scenario where multi-agent collaboration provides meaningful value compared with a straightforward single-agent solution.

● Demonstrate at least one complete **end-to-end user scenario**.

● Show meaningful coordination among agents during the workflow.

● Submit a project repository with basic setup/run instructions and required dependencies.

Teams may satisfy the implementation requirement by either:

● Creating a reusable Swarm Skill with JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm, together with a working demonstration of the skill; or

● Directly implementing a customized multi-agent application on top of JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm.

Your application should demonstrate several aspects of multi-agent collaboration, such as:

○ Task decomposition

○ Role specialization

○ Agent-to-agent communication

○ Parallel or sequential collaboration

○ Tool or Skill invocation

○ Intermediate-result sharing

○ Dynamic replanning or task reassignment

○ Review, verification, or quality control

○ Failure handling or fallback behavior

The collaboration does **not** need to use all of these mechanisms.

What matters is that multiple agents contribute meaningfully to solving the task rather than acting as independent wrappers around the same prompt.

---

## Using JiuwenSwarm and WorkSwarm

Teams are **encouraged, but not required**, to use [JiuwenSwarm](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm) or its latest official successor, [WorkSwarm](https://openjiuwen.com/en/workswarm), as the reference framework.

**WorkSwarm is the latest official upgrade of JiuwenSwarm. Teams starting new projects should consider using WorkSwarm where its capabilities and APIs are suitable for their application. Teams may also continue using JiuwenSwarm when following the challenge examples, existing documentation, or compatibility requirements.**

JiuwenSwarm and WorkSwarm are designed for complex tasks that benefit from multi-agent collaboration, including scenarios where a Leader or coordinator decomposes a goal, assembles specialized teammates, coordinates execution, invokes tools and Skills, and integrates results.

Teams may:

● Build an application directly with JiuwenSwarm

● Build a new application with WorkSwarm

● Extend JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm with new agents, tools, Skills, or collaboration mechanisms

● Create a specialized workflow on top of either framework

● Integrate either framework with external APIs, applications, databases, services, or models

● Experiment with new agent coordination or verification mechanisms

● Build using another multi-agent framework while demonstrating the collaboration principles of this challenge

Projects are **not expected to modify the core framework code** unless doing so is useful for the team's idea.

Teams may choose one of the following approaches:

### Reusable Swarm Skill

Teams can define a reusable Swarm Skill that captures a general multi-agent collaboration pattern. This approach is especially suitable when the same team structure and workflow can be applied to multiple related tasks.

### Customized Multi-Agent Application

Teams can directly build a customized application on top of JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm. This approach is especially suitable when the application requires domain-specific agents, tools, interfaces, data sources, or orchestration logic.

Both approaches are equally acceptable. Teams should choose the approach that best fits their project goals.

---

## Creating a Reusable Swarm Skill

Strong multi-agent systems should not need to reinvent their collaboration strategy every time a similar task appears.

Teams that identify a generalizable collaboration pattern may package it as a reusable Swarm Skill. This is optional, but it can make the project easier to extend, share, and apply to new scenarios.

A Swarm Skill captures **how a team of agents works together**, rather than only describing what an individual agent can do.

For example, instead of building a research demo whose agents are hard-coded specifically for one question, a team could extract a reusable:

**Research Team Swarm Skill**

that defines:

● A coordinator that decomposes the research problem

● Multiple researchers that investigate different aspects in parallel

● A critic that checks evidence and identifies inconsistencies

● A synthesizer that combines validated results

● Quality gates for missing or conflicting evidence

● Failure handling when a researcher or external tool fails

Such a collaboration pattern could then be reused for many research tasks.

A standard JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm Swarm Skill may include:

```text
your-team-skill/
├── SKILL.md
├── roles/
│   ├── coordinator.md
│   ├── researcher.md
│   └── reviewer.md
├── workflow.md
├── bind.md
└── dependencies.yaml
```

These components describe:

● **SKILL.md** — what the team can accomplish and when the collaboration should be used

● **roles/** — responsibilities, capabilities, boundaries, and output expectations for each agent role

● **workflow.md** — how agents interact, including sequential or parallel stages and quality gates

● **bind.md** — resource constraints, behavioral rules, exception handling, and degraded modes

● **dependencies.yaml** — tools, Skills, and external capabilities required by the team

Teams may additionally create executable orchestration where appropriate.

Creating a Swarm Skill is **optional**. Teams may instead directly implement a customized multi-agent application on top of JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm.

---

## Judging Criteria

Projects will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

### 1. Multi-Agent Collaboration — 30%

Does the project make meaningful use of multiple agents?

We will consider:

● Quality of task decomposition

● Clarity and usefulness of agent roles

● Whether different agents contribute genuinely different capabilities or perspectives

● Agent communication and information sharing

● Parallel and/or sequential coordination

● Dynamic adaptation based on intermediate results

● Conflict resolution or result integration

● Verification and quality-control mechanisms

Strong projects should demonstrate that the agents are **working as a team**, rather than simply executing a fixed sequence of unrelated prompts.

---

### 2. Scenario Value & Creativity — 25%

Does the project address a clear and meaningful problem?

We are looking for original applications where collaboration between specialized agents creates an experience or capability that would be difficult to achieve with a simple chatbot.

Strong projects should clearly answer:

**Why does this problem benefit from multiple collaborating agents?**

The application may target enterprise, research, coding, personal productivity, education, science, creative work, or another real-world scenario.

---

### 3. Demo Completeness — 20%

Is the application functional, stable, and demo-ready?

We value a **small but complete multi-agent experience** over a very ambitious system with unfinished components.

The project should demonstrate at least one clear end-to-end workflow, such as:

**User Goal → Task Decomposition → Agent Collaboration → Tool/Skill Execution → Verification → Final Result**

The judges should be able to understand what each major agent contributes and how the team reaches the final result.

Concept-only designs, slide decks, architecture diagrams, or static mockups are **not sufficient**; the core multi-agent workflow must be functional and demonstrable.

For teams submitting a Swarm Skill, the demonstration should show the skill operating on at least one concrete task. For teams building a customized application, the demonstration should show the application's complete multi-agent workflow.

---

### 4. Technical Implementation — 15%

Is the system architecture reasonable and well executed?

We will consider:

● Multi-agent system architecture

● Agent orchestration and lifecycle management

● Tool and API integration

● State/context management

● Agent communication design

● Parallel execution where appropriate

● Reliability and error handling

● Cost and latency awareness

● Technical clarity

Additional consideration may be given to thoughtful implementation of:

● Dynamic agent creation or role assignment

● Adaptive task planning

● Failure recovery or task reassignment

● Human-in-the-loop interaction

● Memory and context sharing

● Privacy and security controls

● Distributed agent execution

● Evaluation-driven coordination

---

### 5. Reusability & Extensibility — 10%

Can the solution grow beyond the hackathon demo?

We will consider:

● Whether the architecture can support additional scenarios

● Whether agent roles and workflows are modular

● Whether tools and Skills can be replaced or extended

● Whether the collaboration strategy is generalizable

● Code quality and ease of reuse

Teams may demonstrate reusability in either of two ways:

● By packaging their collaboration pattern as a reusable Swarm Skill; or

● By designing a modular customized multi-agent application whose agents, workflows, tools, and interfaces can be extended to new scenarios.

A Swarm Skill is **not required** to receive a strong score in this category. Teams should choose the implementation approach that best demonstrates the reusability and extensibility of their project.

---

## What We’re Looking For

A winning project does **not** need to contain a large number of agents.

Two or three agents with clear roles and meaningful collaboration can be much stronger than ten agents performing redundant work.

We are looking for projects with:

● A specific and meaningful real-world scenario

● A clear problem that benefits from multi-agent collaboration

Teams may either create a reusable Swarm Skill or directly implement a customized multi-agent application on top of JiuwenSwarm or WorkSwarm. Both approaches are encouraged, and teams should select the one that best fits their idea.

Teams are encouraged to build a **small but complete collaborative system** rather than maximizing the number of agents or features.

Examples of interesting collaboration patterns include:

**Parallel Specialists**
A coordinator decomposes a problem and sends independent subtasks to specialized agents in parallel before integrating the results.

**Planner → Executor → Reviewer**
One agent creates a plan, another executes it, and another independently verifies the result.

**Research → Critique → Synthesis**
Researchers collect evidence from different perspectives, critics identify gaps or contradictions, and a synthesis agent produces a final answer.

**Developer → Tester → Debugger**
One agent implements a solution, another tests it, and another diagnoses failures and proposes corrections.

**Debate / Cross-Check**
Independent agents form different conclusions or perspectives before comparing reasoning and producing a final decision.

**Dynamic Team Formation**
A coordinator determines which specialists are needed based on the current task instead of always invoking the same set of agents.

These are examples only. Teams are encouraged to invent new collaboration patterns.

Most importantly, we want to see a project that answers one question:

**When AI agents can specialize, communicate, coordinate, and verify each other, what can they accomplish together that a single agent cannot?**

title: Cross-site form can trigger localhost knowledge-to-skill generation
body:
Paired: [GitHub #7744](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/issues/7744) ↔ [GitCode #5040](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/5040)

## Summary

`_handle_file_api_post` (jiuwenswarm/channels/web/app_web.py) dispatches every mutating `/file-api/*` POST route (`skills/upload-temp`, `skills/import`, `skills/create-from-knowledge`, `rebuild-agent-data`, `upload`, `file-content`, `ws-debug-config`) with no Origin, Fetch Metadata, CSRF token, or desktop-token check anywhere in the dispatch chain.

## Impact

A plain HTML form on an attacker-controlled page, submitted via a victim's browser while the local jiuwenswarm web server is running, can trigger any of these routes using only the victim's ambient ability to reach localhost; no cookies or credentials are needed from the attacker's page. `/file-api/skills/create-from-knowledge`, the route named in this report, persists a new generated skill from an attacker-supplied URL with no user confirmation beyond the forged request itself.

A pre-existing `desktop_token` mechanism (`JIUWENSWARM_DESKTOP_TOKEN`, an HttpOnly+SameSite=Lax cookie) exists in this codebase but is wired only into SPA-document navigation, never into this request path, so it provides no protection here regardless of whether it's configured.

## Affected version

Confirmed on current `develop` HEAD.

## Suggested fix

Check the `Sec-Fetch-Site` header (sent automatically by modern browsers) at the top of `_handle_file_api_post`, before any route dispatch, and reject any request where it is present and equal to `cross-site`. A fix is attached as a PR, applied to the shared handler so it covers every mutating route behind it at once.

title: [Feature]:  Let scheduled results start a new channel message
body:
Paired: [GitHub #7811](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/issues/7811) ↔ [GitCode #5066](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/issues/5066)

### 🚀 Background Description

When a channel delivers a scheduled result to its source thread, a cron job has no setting to request a new top-level message. A recurring channel report may therefore remain inside an old thread.

### Design Ideas

Add an optional `post_as_root` boolean to cron jobs. Store it with the job and include it in outbound delivery metadata. A channel that supports threads can omit the source thread when the value is true. Keep the default false.

### Involved Public APIs

Add `post_as_root` to cron creation and update inputs, tool schemas, and the persisted job format. Existing jobs keep their current delivery behavior.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

The Slack connector can use the flag when it sends a scheduled result. Channels without thread support can ignore it. PRs [!7711](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/7711) and [!7681](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/7681) each propose Slack cron targeting.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Test job creation, serialization, update, and delivery after a scheduler reload. Test threaded and top-level Slack delivery with a routing target. Confirm that jobs without the flag still use the source thread.

### Additional Information

On upstream `develop` at `661710be33`, a container reproduction produced:

```
job_post_as_root: <missing>
serialized_post_as_root: <missing>
send_kwargs: {'channel': 'C1', 'text': 'scheduled result', 'thread_ts': '1710000000.000100'}
```

The reproduction constructs a Slack outbound route directly. Upstream needs a separate Slack cron-target change, such as [!7711](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/7711) or [!7681](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/7681), before a stored job can use that route.
